raw_case_text:
This was a case report of a 50-year-old male agriculturist, diagnosed as HIV positive 11/2 years back on antiretroviral therapy (ART), who presented with a 6 month history of asymptomatic skin lesions over his limbs. Physical examination revealed multiple, diffuse, non-ulcerating, papulonodular and non-itchy skin lesions of size 2-18 mm [Figure 1]. History revealed that the lesions first appeared on the feet and then over the hands. There was no history of travel to endemic areas of leishmaniasis. There was no hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy. The laboratory investigations revealed anemia hemoglobin (Hb - 8.3 g/dL). The liver function tests, renal function tests, lipid profile and blood sugar were within the normal limits. The platelet count was 2 lacs/muL and the total leucocyte count was 5,100/muL.
Chest X-ray and ultrasound of abdomen were normal. His CD4 count was 126 cells/muL and HIV viral load was <47 copies/mL. The patient was initially suspected to be having histoplasmosis, which was ruled out by skin biopsy.
Punch biopsy of skin lesions showed sheets of histiocytic cells in the sub epithelial tissue, stuffed with numerous amastigotes of Leishmania. Mild lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate was also noted [Figure 2].
The patient was treated with ketoconazole 200 mg twice a day and 450 mg rifampicin daily for 1 month along with ART (nevirapine, stavudine and lamivudine). The patient improved on treatment but later was lost to follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old HIV-positive male agriculturist presented with a 6-month history of asymptomatic papulonodular skin lesions over his upper and lower extremities.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient noticed painless, non-pruritic papulonodular skin lesions that first appeared on his feet 6 months earlier and subsequently spread to his hands.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with HIV infection 1.5 years prior and maintained on antiretroviral therapy (nevirapine, stavudine, and lamivudine); agriculturist with no history of travel to known leishmaniasis-endemic regions.
subjective.review_of_systems: On antiretroviral therapy (nevirapine, stavudine, lamivudine); negative for pruritus, ulceration, or systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Multiple diffuse, non-ulcerating, non-itchy papulonodular skin lesions measuring 2-18 mm over the feet and hands; no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed anemia (Hb 8.3 g/dL) with normal WBC count (5,100/uL), platelets (200,000/uL), liver function, renal function, lipid profile, and blood glucose. Chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 126 cells/uL and HIV viral load was <47 copies/mL. Punch biopsy of a skin lesion revealed sheets of subepithelial histiocytes stuffed with numerous Leishmania amastigotes alongside a mild lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Cutaneous histoplasmosis was ruled out and atypical diffuse Cutaneous Leishmaniasis in an HIV-coinfected patient was confirmed by skin punch biopsy demonstrating sheets of dermal histiocytes packed with Leishmania amastigotes. Treatment with oral ketoconazole (200 mg twice daily) and oral rifampicin (450 mg once daily) for 1 month alongside continued ART (nevirapine, stavudine, lamivudine) produced clinical improvement before the patient was lost to follow-up.
